name: diagram
description: Interactive Mermaid diagrams and Apache ECharts charts for chat agents, with two-way interaction between you, the agent and the diagram.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Charts of a shell command's output are only available in trusted workspaces.

chatParticipants.name: diagram
chatParticipants.description: Draw, change and explain diagrams and charts

commands.name: new
commands.description: Start a new diagram or chart instead of changing the current one

commands.name: explain
commands.description: Explain the current diagram or chart, or the selected parts

disambiguation.description: The user wants to draw, visualize, update or explain a diagram, such as a flowchart, sequence diagram, class diagram, state machine, entity relationship diagram, architecture overview, mind map, timeline or Gantt chart.
examples: Draw a sequence diagram of the login flow
Visualize the class hierarchy in this file
Make a flowchart of this algorithm
Add error handling to the diagram

disambiguation.description: The user wants to visualize data as a chart, such as a pie chart, bar chart, line chart or scatter plot, with the data given inline, in a file or as the output of a shell command.
examples: Render this data as a pie chart
Bar chart of the lines of code per folder
Plot the CSV file as a line chart
Show the disk usage of these directories as a pie chart

languageModelTools.name: diagram_render
languageModelTools.userDescription: Show a Mermaid diagram or an ECharts chart in an interactive panel
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Renders a Mermaid diagram or an Apache ECharts 6 chart in an interactive panel next to the chat, and reports whether it rendered or the error if it did not. Use Mermaid (the default) for structure and flow: flowchart, sequence, class, state, ER, mind map, timeline, Gantt, ... Use language "echarts" with an ECharts option object as JSON for quantitative data: pie, bar, line, scatter, radar, heatmap, treemap, sankey, ... To chart data in a file or a command's output, use diagram_chart instead. In the panel the user can select nodes or chart items, edit the source and send follow-up requests about the selection; call diagram_getState to see the current source and selection before changing a diagram. To let the user drill into an overview diagram, set clickPrompt; to ask the user a question they answer by clicking nodes, call diagram_pickNodes after rendering. Always pass the complete diagram, not a diff. Avoid click directives, HTML, hard-coded colors, backgrounds and fonts: the panel follows the VS Code theme and fits charts to its size.

source.description: The complete diagram, without a surrounding code fence: Mermaid source, or for language "echarts" an ECharts option object as strict JSON (no functions; use string templates such as "{b}: {c}" for formatters).

language.description: How the source is written. Defaults to "mermaid".

title.description: A short title for the diagram, shown in the panel.

clickPrompt.description: Optional. Makes the diagram explorable: a single click on a node or chart item immediately sends this request to the chat on the user's behalf, with {label} replaced by the node's label or the chart item's name, e.g. "Explain {label} in more detail". Use it for overview diagrams the user may want to learn more about part by part.

languageModelTools.name: diagram_chart
languageModelTools.userDescription: Render data, inline, from a file or from a command's output, as a chart in the diagram panel
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Renders data as a chart (Apache ECharts) in the interactive diagram panel next to the chat. Give the data in exactly one way: inline (data), as a workspace file (file: CSV, TSV, JSON or whitespace-separated columns), or as a shell command whose output is the data (command, run in the first workspace folder after the user confirms; e.g. "du -s *" or "git shortlog -sn HEAD"). Use it for requests like 'render this as a pie chart', 'plot sales.csv' or 'bar chart of the lines of code per folder'. The data is parsed into columns (a header row is detected), the label column and numeric value columns are picked automatically unless given, and the result tells you how the data was read. The user can reload a chart of a file or command with Refresh. For charts that need full control, write an ECharts option and use diagram_render with language "echarts" instead.

type.description: The chart type. horizontalBar suits long labels; scatter plots the first two value columns against each other.

title.description: A short title for the chart, shown in the panel.

data.description: Inline data: CSV, TSV, JSON (an array of objects or arrays, or an object mapping names to numbers) or whitespace-separated columns.

file.description: A file with the data, absolute or relative to the first workspace folder.

command.description: A shell command whose standard output is the data, run in the first workspace folder. The user is asked to confirm it.

format.description: How the data is formatted. Detected automatically by default.

labelColumn.description: The column with the labels (categories or slice names), by its header or its generated name such as "Column 2". Defaults to the first text column.

valueColumns.description: The columns with the values, one series each. Defaults to all numeric columns.

sort.description: Sorts the rows by the first value column.

limit.description: Keeps only the first rows, after sorting. A pie or doughnut chart sums up the rest as "Other".

options.description: An ECharts option object deep-merged into the generated option, for fine-tuning, e.g. {"series": [{"label": {"show": false}}]}. Avoid colors, backgrounds and fonts.

clickPrompt.description: Optional. A single click on a chart item immediately sends this request to the chat on the user's behalf, with {label} replaced by the item's name, e.g. "Which files make {label} so large?".

languageModelTools.name: diagram_getState
languageModelTools.userDescription: Read the diagram shown in the diagram panel, with your edits and selection
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns the source (Mermaid, or an ECharts option as JSON) of the diagram or chart currently shown in the interactive diagram panel, whether the user has edited it by hand, whether it fails to render, and which nodes or chart items the user has selected. Call it before changing an existing diagram or chart, and when the user refers to 'this', 'these' or 'the selected' parts of the diagram.

languageModelTools.name: diagram_pickNodes
languageModelTools.userDescription: Ask you to click nodes in the diagram panel, and wait for your answer
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Asks the user to click one or more nodes (or chart items) in the diagram or chart shown in the diagram panel, and waits until they do. Returns the label and id of the picked nodes, or that the user cancelled. Use it when the answer to your question is a part of the diagram, e.g. 'Which part would you like to learn more about?' or 'Which step is failing?'. Render the diagram with diagram_render or diagram_chart first. The prompt is shown above the diagram, so keep it to one short question.

prompt.description: The question shown above the diagram, e.g. 'Which part would you like to learn more about?'

multiple.description: Whether the user may pick several nodes, confirming with a Done button. Defaults to false: the first click answers.
